title: Codex generated the code and visuals of my orbital strategy game. Here is one shared-fuel decision.
author: va2k0r
selftext:
I'm the developer of DeltaV. Codex generated the original game code and visual assets under my direction, including the simulation, interface, spacecraft and planetary environments. I didn't import ship models. The 3D visuals are built through code too.



The clip shows the decision I want players to understand: every ship draws from the same fuel reserve. A transfer affects what is left for the other ships, missile defense and holding contested orbits.



For the AI workflow, I keep the simulation headless and separate from Three.js. Changes to camera, lighting or mesh generation cannot own fuel spending or combat rules. I can test the simulation separately, then check whether the rendered game communicates those rules clearly. Those are two different checks: a correct calculation does not guarantee that a new player understands the decision.



I design the rules, direct iterations, test and review the results. Music is separately licensed; third-party fonts, source sound recordings and libraries are credited separately. No generative AI runs during play.



For anyone generating both code and visuals: how do you check whether the UI explains the underlying system, beyond checking that the code works?



The free guided demo is on Steam for Windows and Apple Silicon Macs. DeltaV is participating in Next Fest, October 19-26; the full game is still in development.
